about.title: Pico Rivera Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause harm quietly — a faulty appliance in a Rosemead Boulevard apartment, a malfunctioning tool used near Whittier Boulevard, a car part that fails on Slauson Avenue. Unlike many personal injury matters, California product liability claims often rest on strict liability: the person hurt generally needs to show the product had a defect — in design, manufacturing, or warning label — and that the defect caused the injury, without having to prove anyone acted negligently. That distinction matters for Pico Rivera residents dealing with medical bills and lost time from work while trying to figure out who's responsible: a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer along the supply chain. Keeping the product itself, along with packaging, receipts, or instructions, can matter a great deal later. Our team reviews product defect claims in Pico Rivera and helps explain your options under California law.

items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any warnings intact can be important evidence, and our team can advise on how to protect it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often use strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that someone was negligent. We can review the specifics of your situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This preserved evidence can matter a great deal if a claim moves forward. Avoid repairing or discarding it.
